cards.text: All through Isaiah 48, the LORD has been speaking to Jacob, to Israel, the people He called. Now He calls for their ears once more: Listen to Me. Friend, when God says that, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Before anything else, how does the LORD tell Israel who He is?

answers.text: A god of the high hills

cards.text: Then He backs it up: His own hand founded the earth, and His right hand spread out the heavens. Friend, I spread out ONE cookie sheet this morning and it took me three tries.

cards.question: When the LORD summons the earth and the heavens, what do they do?

cards.text: Now He tells all of them to come together and listen, and He asks one question: "Which of the idols has foretold these things?" Go ahead, idols. Papa Dorin will wait.

cards.question: True or false: One of the idols foretold the things the LORD is talking about.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about someone He has picked: the LORD's chosen ally. Friend, this ally isn't on the team to hand out the cookie boxes at the door. He's got a JOB.

cards.question: The LORD's chosen ally will carry out His desire against which place?

cards.text: And the LORD wants no confusion about whose idea this was: "I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him." That's like the big boss walking over and signing your paperwork HIMSELF.

cards.question: About His chosen ally, the LORD says: I have brought him, and he will ___ in his mission.

cards.text: Then He says come near and listen, the third time in this passage He's asked for their ears. That's about how many beeps it takes before I notice my oven timer.

cards.question: True or false: From the beginning, the LORD has kept what He says a secret.

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of it, a new voice speaks up. Plot twist, friend: somebody else is talking now, and he says he's been sent.

cards.question: The new speaker says he comes accompanied by His Spirit. Who does he say has sent him?

cards.text: Now it's the LORD again, the One the passage calls their Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel. He says He's the God who teaches them for their benefit.

cards.question: Besides teaching them, what else does the LORD say He does for Israel?

answers.text: Directs them in the way to go
Lets them pick their own road

cards.text: Then come two sad words: if only they had paid attention to His commandments. It's the GPS saying turn left for an hour while you keep going STRAIGHT.

cards.question: If only they had paid attention to His commandments, what does the LORD say would have been like a river and like waves of the sea?
True or false: In that same if only, the LORD says Israel's descendants would have been as countless as the sand.

cards.text: Then the message flips: leave Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, Babylon's own people! If anybody had yelled that into my old junk drawer, I'd have been gone before the dead batteries I shared it with even woke up.

cards.question: How are they told to announce that they're leaving Babylon?
The news goes out to the ends of the earth: The LORD has ___ His servant ___.

cards.text: Then comes a picture from the road: the LORD leading them through the deserts. Not a map, not a guidebook, friend. HIM.

cards.question: True or false: When the LORD led them through the deserts, they went thirsty.

cards.text: He made water flow for them from the rock: He split the rock, and water gushed out. Friend, I can't even get my bakery faucet to stop DRIPPING.
And the LORD closes with one short line. After all that talk of peace like a river, I think this one lands heavy.

cards.question: Who does the LORD say has no peace?

findings.problem: Stop 2 repeats stop 1's question-type pattern exactly. Both stops run multiple choice, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice. Both stops also split 4 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank, so multiple choice dominates each stop.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Now He tells all of them...", "Go ahead, idols." and "Papa Dorin will wait."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then the LORD talks about someone He has picked...", "Friend, this ally isn't on the team..." and "He's got a JOB."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Nothing earlier sets up an ally handing out cookie boxes at a door, and the image doesn't match the core action of being chosen and called for a mission. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "The LORD wants no confusion about whose idea this was" gives a reason for the LORD's words (Isa 48:15) that the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The rest of verse 19, "their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence," is never told or asked. It is part of what Israel would have had if they had paid attention.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Babylon's own people" spends card words explaining the hard word "Chaldeans." It also states an outside fact with no reference.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The question says they announce that they're leaving Babylon. In Isaiah 48:20, what is declared is "The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!" The text doesn't say the announcement is about leaving, so the card adds a connection the text doesn't make. The question also uses "they" without saying who.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then comes a picture from the road...", "Not a map, not a guidebook, friend." and "HIM."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The comparison uses the opposite action. The fact is making water flow from a rock, but the joke is about failing to stop a faucet from dripping.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
